# Native development

`task run:native` runs the Student process on macOS while it uses the shared
Docker PostgreSQL and NATS infrastructure. It does not start application
containers, migrations, or any sibling service.

## Contract

| Concern | Native value |
| --- | --- |
| HTTP listener | `127.0.0.1:18084` by default; override with `STUDENT_NATIVE_HTTP_PORT` |
| PostgreSQL | `127.0.0.1:5432`, database `lw_student`, role `lw_student` |
| NATS | `nats://127.0.0.1:4222` |
| Course | `http://127.0.0.1:18083` by default; override with `STUDENT_NATIVE_COURSE_URL` |
| User | `http://127.0.0.1:18082` by default; currently unused by Student source |
| Optional peers | Disabled unless their corresponding `STUDENT_NATIVE_*_URL` override is set |

The default native port is a proposal for the shared D8 registry. The
orchestrator owns registry assignment; use `STUDENT_NATIVE_HTTP_PORT` if it
selects a different free port.

`HTTP_BIND_ADDRESS` defaults to an empty value for Docker and existing local
usage, retaining the prior all-interface listener. The native adapter sets it
to `127.0.0.1`; it does not add topology branching to handlers or use cases.

## Prerequisites

Start and verify shared infrastructure from
`learning-platform-infrastructure` using its native-infrastructure commands.
The adapter loads that repository's `.env` for its child process, never prints
those values, and derives the Student service DSN from the existing
`LW_STUDENT_DB_*`/`LW_POSTGRES_PASSWORD` variables. Do not put infrastructure
credentials in this repository.

## Commands

```bash
task migrate:status:native
task migrate:native
task run:native
```

The migration command uses the same sorted `db/migrations/*.sql` source in
native, Docker, and CI. It creates `student_schema_migrations` as a checksum
ledger and refuses to adopt a nonempty Student schema that lacks that ledger.
There are no down migrations; `task migrate-down` is destructive and is not a
native-development command.

For standalone Docker parity:

```bash
task up
curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8081/not-found
task down
```

`task up` starts only this Compose file's PostgreSQL and NATS, applies the same
migration command, creates the Student-required `TEACHER_EVENTS` and
`TASKANSWER_EVENTS` streams, then starts Student. Its host mapping is loopback
only and uses `STUDENT_DOCKER_HTTP_PORT` when `8081` is occupied. `task down`
retains the service-specific `pgdata` volume.

Standalone Compose creates the service-local `ms-go-student-net` by default.
For an existing cross-service Docker network, set
`STUDENT_COMPOSE_EXTERNAL_NETWORK=true` and
`STUDENT_COMPOSE_NETWORK=<existing-network-name>`.

## Native proof boundaries

Successful startup proves PostgreSQL connectivity, Core NATS subscriptions,
and the durable Teacher JetStream subscription. A safe Student read such as
`GET /api/v1/student/courses` needs `X-User-ID` and `X-User-Role: STUDENT`; it
reads `student_course_assignment` and does not write application data. Course,
FileStorage, Sandbox, Practice, Validation, and AI calls occur only in their
specific application flows. Set the documented endpoint override before
exercising one of those flows.

## Testing Policy disposable database commands

The authoritative next-action reader uses
`STUDENT_NATIVE_PRACTICE_RUNTIME_URL` and the infrastructure's existing
`LW_PRACTICE_RUNTIME_INTERNAL_TOKEN`. The native adapter exports these as
`PRACTICE_RUNTIME_URL`/`PRACTICE_RUNTIME_INTERNAL_TOKEN`; the Practice catalog
URL remains a separate boundary. An absent or unavailable Runtime reader yields
an explicit waiting decision for active required Practice.

The Testing Policy commands `test:integration:deps` and `test:migration` use
`scripts/test-policy-postgres.py` with the registered logical command as its sole
argument. The wrapper requires approval to start dependencies, uses the pinned
Docker toolchain from its command-specific descriptor, and creates a unique
Compose project from `test/fixtures/policy-postgres.compose.yml`.

One PostgreSQL instance owns `fullschema_student_test` for `DATABASE_URL` and
`student_migration_test` for `STUDENT_MIGRATIONS_TEST_DATABASE_URL`. The canonical
`cmd/ms-student-migrate up` and `status` commands prepare and verify the first
database. The second starts empty and enables the existing explicit schema-reset
opt-in. Both endpoints use the generated loopback port. No development environment
file is loaded. Compose uses a private empty regular environment file in the
owned temporary project directory. All PostgreSQL and database fallback variables
are cleared before binding the generated endpoints. Every migration must be a
regular tracked HEAD SQL file with matching content and mode; the canonical CLI
applies a private immutable copy of that entire set. The destructive migration suite cannot reset the persistence
tests' database.

The wrapper runs the full registered integration package or the existing migration
selector, then removes only its generated project and volumes. Start, SQL
readiness, schema preparation, tests, and cleanup have process-group deadlines.
Cleanup is registered before start, runs on failure or interruption, and its
failure fails the command. Endpoints and credentials are redacted from output.

These suites remain `PARTIAL`. The separate lesson-completion proof database and
NATS bootstrap opt-ins remain unconfigured; their existing coverage exceptions
continue to apply. A successful ordinary CI job does not prove these dependency
suites passed. The policy workflow records actual Docker runtime versions and
checksum-bound provisioner identities before execution.

## PHP validator origin

`PHP_VALIDATOR_URL` is optional and accepts only `scheme://host[:port]` with HTTP or HTTPS, for example `http://localhost:8090`. The Student adapter appends the provider-owned `/api/v1/validate/syntax` route. Paths (including a trailing slash), credentials, queries, and fragments are rejected; API-root overrides must be replaced with the service origin. Empty configuration retains the existing unavailable error when PHP validation is requested. Requests remain POST JSON containing `code`, with a 30-second timeout and the existing response/error mapping.
